statement.p: Fill in the missing values in the table given if you know that dy/dt=0.8 y. Assume the rate of growth given by dy/dt is approximately constant over each unit time interval and that the initial value of y is 5.

static.solution:
t=0 the value of y is 5. Since we are told that dy/dt=0.8 y, we know that at time t=0 the derivative of y is 0.8 (5) = 4. Thus as t goes from 0 to 1, y will increase by 4, so at t=1, y=5 + 4 = 9.
Likewise, at t=1, we get {dy}/{dt} = 0.8 (9)=7.2 so that at t=2, we obtain y=9 + 7.2 = 16.2.
At t=2, we have dy/dt=0.8 (16.2)=12.96 so that at t=3, we obtain y=16.2 + 12.96 = 29.16.
Continuing similarly, dy/dt|_{t=3} = 23.328, so that at t=4 we have y = 29.16 + 23.328 = 52.488.
